title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google

facts.fact: Businesses that have a physical location customers can visit, or that travel to customers where they are, can create a Business Profile on Google.
facts.quote: If your business either has a physical location that customers can visit, or travels to customers where they are, you can create a Business Profile on Google.

facts.fact: Google's guidelines state there should be only one Business Profile per business, because multiple profiles can cause display problems on Google Maps and Search.
facts.quote: There should only be one profile per business, as this can cause problems with how your information displays on Google Maps and Search.

facts.fact: Business descriptions on Google Business Profile may not contain any links of any type.
facts.quote: No links of any type are allowed.

facts.fact: Business descriptions may not focus on special promotions, prices, or offer sales.
facts.quote: Focus on special promotions, prices, and offer sales.

facts.fact: Including unnecessary information in a Business Profile name is not permitted and could result in suspension of the profile.
facts.quote: Including unnecessary information in your business name isn't permitted, and could result in the suspension of your Business Profile.

facts.fact: Trademark or registered signs (such as ®) are not acceptable in a Business Profile name; for example, 'Burger King ®' is not acceptable while 'Burger King' is.
Phone numbers and website URLs are not acceptable in a Business Profile name.

Special characters or legal terms in a Business Profile name require real-world proof, such as signage, business cards, or invoices, that consistently displays those elements as part of the business name.
facts.quote: you must provide real-world proof (e.g.signage, business cards, invoices) that consistently displays those elements as part of your business name.

facts.fact: Fully capitalized words in a business name are not acceptable; 'SUBWAY' is listed as not acceptable while 'Subway' is acceptable.

Merchants may post their own business's contact information, such as social media handles, email, and phone number, on their profile or in responses to reviews and Q&A, but soliciting personal or confidential information is not allowed.
facts.quote: Merchants are permitted to post contact information (social media handles, email, phone number) for their own business
